quandoUsar: An asset page that shows, on the same chart, the closing-price history and analyst targets (high, median, and low) for a future date.
When the reader compares scenarios: hovering or focusing a label brings that target to the front, and a click keeps it highlighted.
When the distance from the last close matters: each label shows the target price and the percentage change relative to it.
quandoEvitar: Use `line-chart` when there is only history, with no targets, or several series to compare.
Use `candlestick-chart` when the reader needs the open, high, low, and close of each period.
Projections with more or fewer than three scenarios don't fit: the component takes exactly `high`, `median`, and `low`.

teclado.acao: With focus on the history, steps back one close and shows the date and price in the tooltip.
Steps forward one close.
Move forward or back ten closes.
Go to the first or last close.
On a target label, pin that scenario as highlighted; press again to release.
Closes the history tooltip.

acessibilidade: The SVG has `role="img"` with the `label` and a hidden summary (last close and the three targets); the history is a `role="slider"` whose `aria-valuetext` reads the date and price.
Each target is a `<button>` with `aria-pressed`, named with price and change; the highlighted target in the header sits in an `aria-live="polite"` region.
The fixed texts (`Last close`, `Today`, `High`, `Median`, `Low`) and the screen-reader names are in English, with no translation prop; `locale` only changes numbers and dates.
movimento: On entering the viewport, the history line draws up to the last close; then the cone and the three dashed lines spring open from it and the labels appear in sequence.
A ring pulses continuously on the last close; the crosshair and tooltip glide on a spring between closes, and new `targets` make the fan glide to the new values.
With “reduced motion” on, everything appears in its final state, the pulse is turned off, and the crosshair jumps from one point to the next.
responsivo: The width follows the container and the height is fixed by `height` (300 px by default); the label column on the right reserves at least 72 px.
On touch, dragging horizontally scans the history and the vertical gesture keeps scrolling the page; below 400 px of container width the header numbers shrink.
notasIA: Pass `history` (`{ date: "YYYY-MM-DD", value }`), `targets` (`{ high, median, low }`), and `label`; without `targetDate`, the horizon is one year after the last close.
Keep `history` referentially stable (a constant or `useMemo`): a new array on every render makes the line redraw each time.
`activeTarget` with `onActiveTargetChange` controls the pinned scenario (`null` = none); for values in reais, pass `currency="BRL"` and `locale="pt-BR"`.

quandoUsar: A short list where the order is the data itself: the day's priorities, steps in a flow, fields in a form.
When the user should reorder by dragging the handle, with mouse or finger, and also by keyboard with the arrow keys.
quandoEvitar: Use `sortable-data-table` when the order comes from a column's value, not from a manual choice.
Rows with their own content (controls, images, several columns) don't fit: each item shows only `title` and `detail`.
Moving items between lists or columns, as in a kanban board, is out of scope: there is a single vertical list here.

teclado.acao: With focus on the handle, move the item one position up or down; focus stays on the same handle.
Move from one handle to the next.

acessibilidade: The list is a `<ul>` with an `aria-label` coming from `label`; each handle is a `<button>` whose name carries the title, the current position, and the instruction to use the arrow keys.
After a keyboard move, focus is returned to the moved item's handle, because reordering swaps the nodes' places in the DOM.

The handle's name is hardcoded in English (“Reorder [title]. Position 2 of 5. Use arrow keys.”) and there is no `aria-live` region announcing the new position; since the code lives in your project, translate it there.
movimento: When the handle is pressed, the row lifts: it scales to 1.02 and gains a shadow that enters by opacity; on release, it settles into place with a short spring.
The other rows slide to make room, and the position number rolls in the direction the row moved.
With “reduced motion” on, the row still follows the pointer but drops straight into place, with no scale, and the number changes without rolling.
responsivo: The list takes the full width of the parent; title and detail are truncated with an ellipsis instead of wrapping.
The handle is 40 px on a side and has `touch-action: none`: dragging by it on a phone doesn't scroll the page, and the rest of the row keeps scrolling normally.
desempenho: All rows stay in the DOM, each with a layout animation, and there is no virtualization; keep the list short.
notasIA: It is controlled and has only a named export: `import { ReorderableList } from "@/components/ryan-ui/reorderable-list/reorderable-list"`, with `items` in the parent's state and `onReorder={setItems}`.
Each item needs a unique, stable `id` and a `title`; `detail` is optional, and `label` gives the list its name for screen readers.
`onReorder` receives the array already in the new order on every position change, including mid-drag, not just on release: keep it in state and defer saving to the server.

quandoUsar: Showing the daily return of a portfolio, fund, or strategy over several months, with each month's total next to its name.
When the pattern matters more than the curve: streaks of good or bad days, the best and worst day, how many days closed up.
As a trading-day picker to drill down elsewhere on the screen, with `onSelectDate`.
quandoEvitar: Use `activity-heatmap` for unsigned daily counts, such as contributions or visits over a year.
Use `calendar` or `date-picker` when the user needs to pick any date; here only days with data are clickable.
Use `line-chart` when what matters is the cumulative evolution, not each day in isolation.

teclado.acao: Move focus to the previous or next day with data, crossing months, and show that day's tooltip.
Step back or forward five days with data (seven with `weekends`), which equals one week when there are no holidays in the way.
Go to the first or last day of the period.
Select the focused day; press again to clear the selection.
Closes the tooltip.
Enters the calendar on a single day (the last focused or the most recent) and leaves it.

acessibilidade: The whole is a `role="group"` named by `label`; each month is a `<section>` with month and total in its name, and each day with data is a `<button>` with `aria-pressed`.
Focus uses a roving tabindex: only one day is in the `Tab` order and the arrow keys lead to the others; days without data are decorative and outside navigation.
Each day's name carries the full date and the return (`up`, `down`, or `flat` plus the percentage); these terms and the visible labels, such as `Best day` and `Closed`, are hardcoded in English.
movimento: On entering the viewport, the months rise one after another and each month's cells appear in a diagonal wave, growing from half size; the grand total counts up from zero to the value.
The tooltip is a single one: it appears already in place and then glides on a spring from one day to the next; with a mouse, the day under the cursor grows slightly.
With “reduced motion” on, months and cells only fade, the total appears directly, and the tooltip doesn't glide.
responsivo: Months are distributed into columns of at least 128 px according to the container's width; below 420 px they always sit in two columns.
On touch, the tooltip stays visible for about two seconds after the finger leaves, to give time to read.
desempenho: Each day with data is a `<button>` (a year of trading days gives about 250), and the wave entrance uses only CSS transitions with delay, with no JavaScript per cell.
notasIA: Pass `returns` as `{ date: "YYYY-MM-DD", value }`, with `value` in percentage points (`1.2` = +1.2%); days without an entry appear as closed and months without an entry aren't drawn.
Totals are compounded by default: `compound={false}` sums the returns, `weekends` shows Saturday and Sunday, and `scale` fixes the percentage at which the color saturates.

Controlled selection with `selectedDate` and `onSelectDate` (`null` = none) or internal with `defaultSelectedDate`; keep `returns` in `useMemo`, since the whole calendar is recomputed when the array changes.

quandoUsar: Comparing the shape of several distributions at once: daily temperatures by month, response times by region.
When the question is about shift and spread: where each group's median is and how wide the middle half is.
Showing how distributions change between two datasets: with the same `id`s, each curve transforms into the new one.
quandoEvitar: Use `bar-chart` when each group has a single value, not a collection of observations.
Use `line-chart` or `streamgraph` when the horizontal axis is time and you want to see evolution, not distribution.
With few observations per group, the smoothed curve suggests a shape the data doesn't support; prefer showing the values.

teclado.acao: With focus on the chart, pick the previous or next ridge and raise it.
Move the reading cursor along the values, one axis step at a time.
Go to the first or last ridge.
Releases the raised ridge and hides the tooltip.

acessibilidade: The `<figure>` carries the `label`; the chart area is a focusable group with `aria-roledescription="ridgeline chart"` and the keyboard instructions in its name, in English.
An `aria-live="polite"` region reads the active series (median, middle half, range, and count) and, with the cursor, the fraction of values up to that point.
A hidden table lists the median, quartiles, minimum, maximum, and count of each series, so screen readers don't depend on the drawing.
movimento: On entering the viewport, the ridges grow from the baseline in a wave, from top to bottom; when the data changes, each curve and the axis transform on a spring to the new shape.
The ridge under the pointer rises 6 px on a copy drawn on top, with the band between the quartiles highlighted, while the others fade; the tooltip follows the pointer on a spring.
With “reduced motion” on, shapes are painted directly in the final state and the tooltip follows the pointer without a spring.
responsivo: The width follows the container and the height comes from the content: `rowHeight` per series plus the overlap and axis space; there is no total height prop.
Below 420 px of width the name column shrinks from 52 to 36 px, with ellipses, and the axis shows fewer ticks (about one every 72 px).
desempenho: Density is computed in the browser (96 samples per series, each against all observations) and `series` is serialized on every render, including when moving the pointer; with many thousands of values, downsample first.
notasIA: Pass raw observations in `values`, not ready-made densities: the component estimates the curve with Silverman's rule per series, or with `bandwidth` in value units.
Use a stable `id` per series so the curves transform when the data is swapped, and fix `domain` when two datasets need the same axis.
`active` with `onActiveChange` controls the raised ridge; `tint` (on by default) colors each ridge by its median and shows the scale below the chart.

quandoUsar: Showing how a total splits and recombines across two or more stages: traffic source, landing page, and outcome.
When the reader needs to follow a path: pointing at a node lights up its ribbons and the nodes at their ends; pointing at a ribbon lights up the two nodes it connects.
Comparing two periods with the same nodes: when `links` changes, bars and ribbons glide to the new sizes.
quandoEvitar: Use `funnel-chart` when the flow is a single sequence of stages and what matters is the loss between one and the next.
Use `composition-chart` or `donut-chart` when the total splits only once, with no following stages.
Flows that return to an earlier stage don't fit: the layout puts each node in a column, left to right, by the longest path from the source.

teclado.acao: With focus on the chart, move to the previous or next node, column by column.
Jump to the vertically nearest node in the previous or next column.
Go to the first or last node.
Removes the highlight.

acessibilidade: The chart is a focusable vertical `role="slider"`: on receiving focus by keyboard, it highlights the first node, and `aria-valuetext` reads the current node's name, value, and column.
The keyboard moves through nodes only; ribbons respond to the pointer or to `activeId`, and all flows are in a hidden table for screen readers.
The `label` becomes the `<figure>`'s hidden caption; the tooltip texts (`Total`, `To`, `From`, `Flow`) and the slider's name are hardcoded in English.
movimento: The first time on screen, the node bars grow from the center and the ribbons draw out from the source, one column after another.
After that, data changes don't repeat the entrance: nodes, ribbons, and labels that still exist glide on a spring to the new position and thickness.
With “reduced motion” on, everything is drawn directly in the final state and the highlight changes without a transition.
responsivo: The width follows the container and the height is the `height` prop (300 px); columns split the width equally, so many stages in little space squeeze the labels.
When the space between columns tightens, labels switch to `--text-xs` and are truncated with an ellipsis; the value beside the name only appears with 100 px free.
desempenho: The layout is recomputed when `nodes`, `links`, or the width change; keep both arrays stable (a constant or `useMemo`) so it isn't rebuilt on every render.
notasIA: Pass `nodes` (`{ id, label, color? }`) and `links` (`{ source, target, value }`), with a single link per source and target pair: the link's id is `source>target`.
The order of `nodes` sets the stacking of the first column and `columns` provides the titles; nodes with no flow and links with zero or negative value are ignored.
Only the first four nodes in the first column get a series color (`--series-1` through `--series-4`); the rest stay in a neutral tone unless you pass `color`.

quandoUsar: Showing how several items changed between exactly two moments: before and after, one quarter and the next.
When the change in rank counts as much as the value: the arrow beside each final value says how many positions the item rose or fell.
Telling the story of one item among the others: `highlightKey` paints one line in the accent color and leaves the rest neutral.
quandoEvitar: Use `bump-chart` when the ranking changes over three or more periods.
Use `line-chart` when there are intermediate values and the path between the extremes matters.
Use `bar-chart` to compare the items at a single moment, with no before and after.

teclado.acao: With focus on the chart, highlight the next item, in final-value order.
Highlight the previous item.
Go to the first or last item in that order.
Clears the highlight and hides the tooltip.

acessibilidade: The chart area is a focusable group with `aria-roledescription="slope chart"`; on receiving focus by keyboard, it highlights the first item in final-value order.
An `aria-live="polite"` region reads the highlighted item (name, both values, change, and rank change), and a hidden summary and table carry all items.
The rank phrases, such as `up 2 to rank 1`, are hardcoded in English and also appear in the visible tooltip.
movimento: On entering the viewport, the starting points appear in sequence, each line draws from left to right, and only then do the final point and label appear.
When swapping `data` while keeping the same `key`s, lines, points, and labels glide on a spring to the new slope, and the rank-change number rolls to the new value.
With “reduced motion” on, the chart appears ready and data and highlight changes are immediate.
responsivo: The width follows the container; below 440 px the label columns shrink and the text switches to `--text-xs`, with ellipses on long names.
The default height is 44 px per item, with a minimum of 200 px (`height` sets another value); labels that would overlap are pushed apart and tied to the point by a stroke.
notasIA: Pass `data` as `{ key, label, start, end }` and the column titles in `startLabel` and `endLabel`; both sides use the same value axis.
Keep `key` stable between datasets so lines transform instead of vanishing and reappearing; `formatValue` and `formatChange` handle unit and sign.
`activeKey` exists only in the controlled form, with `onActiveChange`; without it the highlight is internal and disappears when leaving the chart, and `ranks={false}` hides the rank arrows.

quandoUsar: Comparing structured records in columns, letting the user sort by any of them: projects, invoices, team members.
Selecting several rows for a bulk action: `selectable` adds the checkbox column, selection by clicking the row, range selection with `Shift`, and the count in the footer.
Tables that fit entirely on the page, where sorting can happen in the browser.
quandoEvitar: Use `tree-table` when rows have children and sorting must respect the hierarchy.
Use `comparison-table` to compare plans or products feature by feature, with one highlighted column.
Large collections or ones sorted on the server call for another solution: sorting is local, all rows go into the DOM, and there is no prop to control the order from outside.

teclado.acao: On a header, sort by the column; again, toggle between ascending and descending.
On a checkbox, check or uncheck the row; on the header checkbox, all rows.
In the header, move focus between the select-all checkbox and the sort buttons.
Move focus between the row checkboxes; from the first row, `↑` goes up to the select-all checkbox, and from it `↓` goes back down.
Go to the first or last header control, or to the first or last row checkbox.
Clears the selection when rows are checked.

acessibilidade: It is a native `<table>` with a hidden `caption` and explicit ARIA roles, which keep the semantics when CSS redraws it on narrow screens; sortable headers carry `aria-sort`.
A `role="status"` region announces the column and direction of the sort and how many rows are selected; the header checkbox uses the indeterminate state.
Each row's checkbox is named by the value of the first column; the fixed texts (`Sort by`, `Select all rows`, `Clear selection`) are in English.
movimento: When sorting, rows glide on a spring to the new position over a fixed band that tints the sorted column; the arrow appears on the column and rotates when the direction flips.
The checkbox mark draws itself and, in the header, morphs between check and dash; the footer count swaps text rising or descending, with the width following.
With “reduced motion” on, rows swap places instantly and texts merely alternate, with no displacement or blur.
responsivo: In windows up to 620 px the header becomes a scrollable strip of sort buttons and each row folds into two: first column and first number on top, the rest below.
The rule is a window media query, not a container query: in a narrow panel on a wide screen the table keeps a 560 px minimum width and scrolls horizontally.
desempenho: There is no pagination or virtualization, and each row is a `motion.tr` with a layout animation: for long collections, slice `rows` and combine with `pagination`.
Column widths are measured once and locked with `table-layout: fixed`, so sorting doesn't cause reflow; the measurement only repeats if the columns change.
notasIA: Pass `rows`, `columns` (`{ key, label, render?, numeric?, width? }`), and `rowKey`; every column is sortable unless it has `sortable: false`.
Sorting uses the raw value of `row[key]`, not what `render` returns: keep numbers and `Date` in the data and format only in `render`; empty values always go last.
Sorting is internal only (`defaultSort` and `onSortChange`); selection can be controlled with `selectedKeys` and `onSelectionChange`, and the first column should identify the row.

quandoUsar: A compact trend with label, current value, and change in a single block, in dashboards with several indicators side by side.
When the series' shape is enough, but the user may still want to read a point: the pointer or arrow keys show that point's value and label.
Indicators that update: new data makes the line transform from the current drawing, even with a different number of points.
quandoEvitar: Use `line-chart` when the reader needs axes, several series, or a legend.
Use `metric-card` when the number, a line of context, and the change are enough, without the series.
Inside a table cell or in the middle of text it doesn't work: the `label` always appears above the line and there is no prop to hide it.

teclado.acao: With focus on the chart, go to the previous point and show its value in the header.
Go to the next point.
Move forward or back about a sixth of the series.
Go to the first or last point.
Ends the reading and returns to the most recent value.

acessibilidade: The `<figure>` has an `aria-label` built from `label`, `value`, and `change`, and the SVG is decorative.
With `interactive` (default), the chart area is a focusable `role="slider"` whose `aria-valuetext` reads the point's label and formatted value; with `interactive={false}` there is no `Tab` stop.
`tone` only changes the color: write sign and unit in `change` and pass `labels`, so each point is read with its date, not as `Point 3 of 14`.
movimento: When half of the component enters the viewport, the line draws from left to right, the fill follows the tip, and the end dot lands on the last value.
While reading, the cursor springs to the point and runs along the line, the stretch after it fades, and the header texts roll digit by digit.
With “reduced motion” on, the line appears ready, the data swap and the cursor jump, and the texts merely alternate.
responsivo: `width` and `height` define only the aspect ratio and the first drawing: the chart takes the container's width, and in a flex row with no defined width it ends up at 300 px, the browser default for an SVG with no size.
On touch, dragging horizontally scans the points and releasing ends the reading; the vertical gesture keeps scrolling the page.
desempenho: Each instance creates up to three `ResizeObserver`s (the chart and the two rolling texts) and rewrites the SVG attributes on every frame while it draws, transforms, or follows the cursor.
notasIA: Pass `data` (numbers) and `label`; `value` and `change` are texts you already supply formatted, and `formatValue` formats the point shown during reading.
Set the width via the parent (a grid column or a wrapper with a width): the `width` prop doesn't fix the on-screen size, only the aspect ratio together with `height`.
When the chart is purely illustrative, `interactive={false}` removes the `Tab` stop and pointer reading, and `area={false}` removes the fill under the line.

quandoUsar: A status page: a service's availability over the last days, one bar per day, with the overall percentage and the current state in the header.
When each day may carry an incident note: the tooltip shows date, state, availability, and the `note` text.
As a day picker to open incident details elsewhere on the screen, with `onSelectDate`.
quandoEvitar: Use `activity-heatmap` for activity volume per day over a year, with no service states.
Use `line-chart` or `sparkline` for a continuous metric, such as latency, instead of one state per day.
States outside the five provided (`operational`, `degraded`, `outage`, `maintenance`, `unknown`) can't be represented.

teclado.acao: Move focus to the previous or next day and show that day's tooltip.
Step back seven days.
Step forward seven days.
Go to the first or last day.
On a day, select or clear the selection; in the legend, pin or release that state's highlight.
Closes the tooltip.

acessibilidade: The strip is a `role="group"` named with the service and the number of days; each day is a `<button>` with `aria-pressed` whose name carries the full date, state, availability, and note.
Focus uses a roving tabindex (a single day in the `Tab` order, initially the most recent); the legend is a group of toggle buttons with each state's day count.
The state names and header phrases (`All systems operational`, `Degraded performance`) are hardcoded in English; only `caption` and the `locale` formats change.
movimento: When half of the strip enters the viewport, the bars rise in a wave from left to right (about half a second in total) and the percentage counts up to the value.

The bar under the pointer stretches and the two neighbors on each side follow it progressively less; the single tooltip glides on a spring between days and a ring pulses endlessly on the current state's point.
With “reduced motion” on, the bars only fade, with no scale, the pulse is turned off, and the percentage appears directly.
responsivo: Bars divide the container's width equally, with a 1 to 3 px gap: many days in a narrow container give very thin bars, so shorten the period on phones.
Below 380 px of container width the percentage shrinks; the tooltip slides sideways to stay inside the component and, on touch, stays visible for about two seconds.
desempenho: Each day is a `<button>`, and the highlight around the pointer is computed in CSS from a variable, with no JavaScript per bar; the cost grows with the number of days.
notasIA: Pass `days` from oldest to most recent (`{ date, status, uptime?, note? }`) and `label` with the service name; the header state is that of the last day.
Without `uptime` on each day, the average uses assumed values per state (99.4 for `degraded`, 96 for `outage`); provide the real value per day or the total in the `uptime` prop.
Despite the name, it isn't an application's status bar: it is a service's availability strip; selection is controlled with `selectedDate` and `onSelectDate`.

quandoUsar: Showing how the mix of several parts changes over time, when the overall shape matters more than exact values: tickets by topic, traffic by channel.
When the reader wants to isolate one part: pointing at a layer or its legend entry fades the others, and the tooltip reads values point by point.
Switching between periods of different lengths: layers are resampled onto a common grid and transform from one dataset to the other.
quandoEvitar: Use `line-chart` when the reader needs to compare exact values across series: here only the layer's thickness is readable, and the baseline undulates.
Use `bump-chart` when what matters is each series' ranking position in each period.
Use `composition-chart` or `donut-chart` for the split of a total at a single moment.

teclado.acao: With focus on the chart, step back or forward one point in time.
Switch the highlighted layer, following the order of `series`.
Move forward or back about a sixth of the period.
Go to the first or last point.
In the legend, hide or show the focused button's layer.
Ends the reading and hides the tooltip.

acessibilidade: The chart area is a focusable group with `aria-roledescription="stream graph"`; on receiving focus by keyboard, reading starts at the most recent point.
An `aria-live="polite"` region reads the current point, the highlighted layer with its value, and the total; a hidden summary and table carry all the data.
The legend is a group of buttons with `aria-pressed` (pressed = layer visible); the table's first column header comes from `categoryLabel`, which defaults to `Date`.
movimento: The first time on screen, the flow opens from a thread along the center; new data makes each layer transform on a spring from its current shape.
Hiding a layer through the legend thins it until it vanishes while the others close the gap; the crosshair glides between points and the tooltip follows on its own spring.
With “reduced motion” on, layers go straight to the final state and the crosshair and tooltip jump.
responsivo: The width follows the container and the height is the `height` prop (260 px); the axis shows at most one `axisLabel` every 72 px, counting from the most recent.
The name inside a layer only appears where it is at least 19 px thick and the text fits; on thin layers, identification is left to the legend and tooltip.
desempenho: Drawing is imperative: on every animation frame all layers have their path rebuilt with 161 samples and the baseline recomputed, so the cost grows with the number of layers.
notasIA: Pass `series` (`{ key, label, color? }`) and `data` with a `values` object per point, indexed by the series `key`; missing or negative values count as zero.

The order of `series` runs from the center outward: the first runs through the middle and the rest alternate above and below; only the first four get a series color, and the rest stay neutral without `color`.
`offset="zero"` stacks from a straight base and `offset="silhouette"` centers the stack; `hiddenSeries` with `onHiddenSeriesChange` controls the hidden layers.

quandoUsar: Highlight cards in a showcase or product page, such as a travel destination or a boarding pass, where depth draws attention to a few items.
When parts of the content should float above the face: each `TiltCardLayer` rises `depth` px during hover and shifts against the background as the card tilts.
quandoEvitar: Use `card` for ordinary cards in lists and panels, where the motion would only distract.
Use `wallet-card` for a payment card that also flips to show the back.
In interfaces used mostly by touch the effect is lost: the card only tilts with a mouse.
acessibilidade: It is a visual container, with no role or focus of its own: if the whole card leads somewhere, put a link or button with the action text inside it.
The tilt only responds to the mouse; keyboard, touch, pen, and screen readers don't perceive it, so no information should depend on it.
The glare is `aria-hidden` and has `pointer-events: none`, so links and buttons beneath it stay clickable.
movimento: The card rotates up to `maxTilt` degrees (10 by default) at the edges, following the cursor with a firm spring and no bounce, scales up to `hoverScale`, and shows a glare at the cursor position.
On leaving, it returns to flat on a spring; the `TiltCardLayer` layers rise with the hover and return to the face at rest, where the text is sharp.
With “reduced motion” on, as with `disabled`, the card stays flat: no rotation, no scale, no glare, and no raised layers.
desempenho: The card keeps `will-change: transform` all the time (except with “reduced motion”), which reserves a compositing layer per instance; in a grid with dozens of them, use the effect only on highlights.
notasIA: Import `TiltCard` (and `TiltCardLayer`, if you want layers) from `@/components/ryan-ui/tilt-card/tilt-card`; set width and height via `className` or `style`, because the inner card fills the container's height.
Every element between the card and the layers needs `transform-style: preserve-3d`, like the boarding pass body in the demo; without it the layers flatten onto the face.
The card doesn't clip its content: for a cover image, use `position: absolute`, `inset: 0`, and `border-radius: inherit`; `onTiltChange` fires on every mouse movement, so avoid heavy state there.

quandoUsar: A project's history, audit log, or sequence of deploys, where order and recency matter more than comparing fields.
Feeds that receive updates while the screen is open: the new event enters at the top, the others move down, and its title is announced to the screen reader.
When only some events have details worth opening: with `detail`, the row becomes a button that expands in place.
quandoEvitar: Use `sortable-data-table` when people need to sort or compare records by column.
Use `stepper` to show the steps of a flow and what is already complete, not dated events.
Use `notification-center` for notices with read and unread state.

teclado.acao: Move focus to the previous or next row that has `detail`; rows without detail don't receive focus.
Go to the first or last row with detail.
Open or close the focused row's detail.

acessibilidade: The feed is a `region` named by `label`; each day is a `<section>` tied to its heading (`role="heading"` at the `headingLevel` level, 3 by default), and events form an ordered list.
Rows with `detail` are `<button>`s with `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls`; the time is a `<time>` with the full date in hidden text, and new events are announced in a `role="status"` region.
`tone` only changes the marker's color: write the outcome in the `title` (“Deploy failed”); the avatar has an empty `alt` because the name already comes in `actor`.
movimento: Each row reveals itself once, on entering the viewport: the marker appears growing and the vertical stroke draws to the next one; rows that appear together enter 90 ms apart.
New events enter at the top, making room while the others move down; the detail opens with a spring on height, the arrow rotates, and the relative time and day count swap by rolling.
With “reduced motion” on, there is no stagger or displacement: markers, strokes, and details appear instantly or with a short fade, and the return to the top is instant.
responsivo: With `maxHeight`, the feed scrolls internally, day headings stick to the top, and the bottom edge fades while there are more events; without it, the feed grows with the page.
If a new event arrives while the feed is scrolled down, it returns to the top on its own; turn this off with `scrollToNew={false}`.
desempenho: There is no virtualization: all events stay in the DOM and each row detects its viewport entry only once; for long histories, limit what is passed in `events`.
notasIA: Pass `events`, `label`, and `now` (epoch ms); the component has no clock of its own, so update `now` from time to time (every minute, for example) so relative times don't go stale.
Days and hours use `timeZone="UTC"` by default: pass the local time zone (`"America/Sao_Paulo"`) and `locale`; “Today”, “Yesterday”, “updates”, and the times `8m` and `Now` stay in English.
Use a stable `id`: it is how an event is recognized as new, animates its entrance, and is announced; on another surface, define `--timeline-surface` for the day headings' background.

quandoUsar: Hierarchical data with columns to compare: folders and files with owner and size, budget by area and sub-area, teams and people.
Bulk selection in a hierarchy: checking a parent checks everything below it, and the parent shows a mixed state when only some children are checked.
Large trees whose children come from the server on open, with `loadChildren`, a loading row, and a retry button when the load fails.
quandoEvitar: Use `tree-view` to navigate a hierarchy by names only, with no data columns.
Use `sortable-data-table` when records have no children.
Thousands of rows open at once call for virtualization, which this component doesn't have.

teclado.acao: Move focus one row up or down; Page Up and Page Down jump ten rows.
Go to the first or last visible row.
→ opens the row or, if it is already open, moves down to the first child; ← closes the row or, if it is already closed, moves up to the parent.
Opens or closes a row with children, calls `onRowActivate` on a leaf, and, after a load failure, retries.
With `selectable`, Space checks or unchecks the row and its descendants; Ctrl + A (⌘ + A on Mac) checks everything or clears the selection.
Opens all sibling rows of the focused row, loading any missing children.

acessibilidade: Follows the `treegrid` pattern: rows have `aria-level`, `aria-posinset`, `aria-setsize`, and `aria-expanded`, and focus is roving, with a single row in the `Tab` order.
With `selectable`, the grid is `aria-multiselectable` and checked rows have `aria-selected`; the checkboxes are outside `Tab` (checking is done with Space) and get their name from `rowLabel`.
An `aria-live` region announces sorting, expanding or collapsing all, and the result of loads; if the focused row disappears when a branch closes, focus moves up to the nearest visible ancestor.
movimento: Opening a row makes the children grow in height on a spring and appear in a slight sequence; closing collapses on the same spring, and the arrow rotates 90°.
When sorting, rows glide to the new position within their level; when children arrive from `loadChildren`, the first takes the loading row's place, with no jolt.
With “reduced motion” on, rows appear and disappear with a short fade, without growing in height; the loading skeleton stops pulsing and the indicator spins more slowly.
responsivo: `hideBelow` hides a column while the table is narrower than that value in px; the measure is of the table itself, so it also applies to narrow panels on wide screens.
With `maxHeight`, the body scrolls internally and the header stays fixed; the row that receives focus by keyboard is scrolled into view without being hidden under the header.
desempenho: Only the rows of open branches go into the DOM, but without virtualization: opening everything in a tree of thousands of nodes renders them all, each with height and position animation.
notasIA: Each row is `{ id, data, children? }`; for on-demand loading, leave `children` undefined, set `hasChildren: true`, and pass `loadChildren`, which returns a `Promise` with the children.

The first column carries the tree; `sortValue` makes the column sortable (ascending, descending, unsorted), `width` accepts a grid track (`"90px"`, `"minmax(0, 2fr)"`), and `align: "end"` aligns numbers.

It depends on the `checkbox` item, installed along with it; `Loading`, `Couldn't load`, and `Retry` are hardcoded in English, and to open everything from outside use `collectExpandableIds(rows)` with `expanded` and `onExpandedChange`.

quandoUsar: Navigating folders and nested content in a side panel: a project's files, sections of documentation, categories of a catalog.
When each node needs only a name and an icon, and the user opens and closes branches to reach an item.
When the tree-pattern keyboard is expected: arrow keys to move, open, and close, and Enter to choose.
quandoEvitar: Use `tree-table` when each node has data columns, multiple selection, or children loaded on demand.
Use `file-tree` for a file explorer with change markers and type-ahead search.
Use `animated-sidebar` for an application's navigation menu, with groups that open and a collapsed icon rail.

teclado.acao: Move focus to the previous or next visible item.
Go to the first or last visible item.
Opens the closed folder; on an open folder, moves focus to the first child.
Closes the open folder; on a file or a closed folder, moves focus to the parent folder.
Select the item and call `onSelect`; on a folder, also open or close it.
Enters the tree on the last focused item and leaves it; the other items are outside the `Tab` order.

acessibilidade: It is a single-selection `role="tree"` in which each row is a `<button>` with `role="treeitem"`, `aria-level`, `aria-posinset`, `aria-setsize`, `aria-selected`, and, on folders, `aria-expanded`.
Focus is roving: only one item is in the `Tab` order, and if it disappears because the folder closed, the stop moves to the first visible item.
The default name is `File tree`, in English: pass an `aria-label` describing the content; icons are decorative (`aria-hidden`).
movimento: When a folder opens, the space opens on a single spring and the new children enter in sequence, sliding from the left; on close, they collapse in height and fade quickly.
The selection background glides from one item to another, the arrow rotates 90°, the icon switches between closed and open folder, and the indent guide grows from top to bottom.
With “reduced motion” on, items appear and disappear with no height or displacement, the selection jumps, and icons swap instantly.
responsivo: Each level indents 18 px and the name is truncated with an ellipsis, so deep trees in a narrow panel leave little room for the text.
desempenho: All items of open folders stay in the DOM, each with entrance, exit, and position animation; folders with hundreds of items should start closed.
notasIA: Pass `nodes` (`{ id, label, children?, icon? }`) and `aria-label`; a node with non-empty `children` becomes a folder, and file icons get a color by extension (`.ts`, `.tsx`, `.css`, `.md`, `.json`).
Expansion can be controlled (`expandedIds` with `onExpandedChange`) or not (`defaultExpandedIds`); selection is always internal, starts empty, and can't be set by a prop.
Clicking a folder also selects it and calls `onSelect`: if only files should open content, check `node.children` in the handler.

quandoUsar: Showing a hierarchy of parts of a whole, such as revenue by business line and product, when relative size matters more than exact comparisons.
Exploring by levels: clicking a block zooms that branch to fill the view, and the breadcrumb at the top goes back to any level above.
Showing a second measure, such as growth, in color intensity, with `colorLabel` and a stepped scale below the chart.
quandoEvitar: Use `bar-chart` when the reader needs to compare values precisely: areas are hard to compare by eye.
Use `composition-chart` or `donut-chart` for a few parts at a single level.
Use `tree-table` when each node of the hierarchy needs exact numbers in columns.

teclado.acao: With focus on the chart, jump to the nearest first-level block in that direction.
Go to the first or last first-level block, in the order of `data`.
Zoom into the focused block, when it has children, and move the highlight to the first child.
Go up one level and highlight the block it came from; at the root, remove the highlight.

acessibilidade: The block area is a focusable group with `aria-roledescription="treemap"` and the instructions in its name, in English; the keyboard moves through the first-level blocks of the view only.
An `aria-live="polite"` region reads the active block (path, value, share of its parent, and the color measure), and a hidden table lists all nodes with path and values.
The breadcrumb is a `<nav>` with an ordered list and `aria-current="location"` on the current level; the tooltip is decorative (`aria-hidden`).
movimento: The first time on screen, blocks grow from their own center, in a quick wave that starts with the largest.
When zooming in, the chosen block grows to fill the view and the children appear; when going back, the view shrinks to it; with new data, each block resizes in place.
With “reduced motion” on, each change goes straight to the final layout, the tooltip doesn't glide, and the breadcrumb swaps without displacement.
responsivo: The width follows the container and the height is fixed by `height` (420 px); name and value only appear on blocks with room (over 64 × 38 px), and small ones depend on the tooltip.
On touch there is no hover tooltip: tapping a block zooms into its branch, and tapping a first-level leaf shows its numbers.
desempenho: Every node in the tree has a DOM element, even out of view, `data` is serialized on every render, and the animation repositions blocks in JavaScript on every frame; with thousands of leaves, aggregate first.
notasIA: Pass a root in `data` (`{ id, label, children }`) with `value` only on leaves: a branch's value is the sum of its children, and the root's `label` starts the breadcrumb.
To color by the second measure, give `color` to the leaves and pass `colorLabel` (and `formatColor`); the first four branches get a series hue and the rest stay neutral.
`focus` with `onFocusChange` controls the zoomed branch (a leaf id shows the root); keep the `id`s stable between datasets so blocks transform instead of reappearing.

quandoUsar: Showing at which prices trading concentrated in a session or a few sessions, alongside how the price moved over time.
Highlighting the point of control, the level with the most volume, and the value area, which by default gathers 70% of the volume around it.
Reading each price band with its volume, share of the total, and position relative to the value area, by pointer or arrow keys.
quandoEvitar: Use `candlestick-chart` when the focus is the open, high, low, and close of each period.
Use `order-book` for the depth of open buy and sell orders, not for what has already traded.
Use `bar-chart` for volume per period, such as per day or per hour; here volume is grouped by price.

teclado.acao: With focus on the chart, move up to the next price band.
Move down to the previous band.
Move up or down four bands.
Go to the lowest or highest price band.
Ends the reading and hides the tooltip.

acessibilidade: The chart is a vertical `role="slider"`: on receiving focus by keyboard it starts at the point of control, and `aria-valuetext` reads the band, the volume, the share of the total, and whether it is in the value area.
The `<figure>` has a hidden caption and a hidden table with all bands, from highest to lowest, with volume and share; the SVG, header, and tooltip are hidden from screen readers.
The read-out phrases and the header (`point of control`, `Inside the value area`, `Value area`) are hardcoded in English; `formatPrice` and `formatVolume` change only the numbers.
movimento: On entering the viewport, the bars grow from the axis, starting at the point of control and spreading to the farthest levels, while the price line draws from left to right.
After that, new data doesn't repeat the entrance: bars, line, and the point-of-control mark glide on a spring, and a series with a different number of points redraws the line from the start.
With “reduced motion” on, everything appears in its final state, and the highlighted band and the tooltip jump from one level to the next.
responsivo: The width follows the container: the histogram takes 32% of it (between 64 and 190 px), the price line takes the rest, and a fixed 62 px column on the right holds the prices; the height is `height` (260 px).
On touch, tapping at a height reads that band; dragging vertically scrolls the page and ends the reading.
desempenho: The price line is rebuilt on every render, including when the pointer changes band; with thousands of trades, aggregate into intervals first, as the demo does with 5 and 15 minutes.
notasIA: Pass `data` in time order with `{ key, label, price, volume }` and `axisLabel` on only some points; each point adds its volume to the band the price falls in, and `levels` (16) sets how many bands there are.

`valueArea` (0.7) is the fraction of volume that forms the value area; `formatPrice` and `formatVolume` format the axis, header, and tooltip, and `hideHeader` hides the title with the point of control.
`activeLevel` with `onActiveChange` controls the band being read, counted from the lowest price (0), or `null` for none; without control, `defaultActiveLevel` sets the initial one.

quandoUsar: Showing parts of a whole as countable squares, where each cell is worth one percent: energy mix, survey responses, budget by area.
Comparing two moments with the same categories: when `data` changes, cells that change group fly to their new place and the legend rolls the percentages.
When color can't be the only channel: besides color, categories alternate between square, round, and framed cells.
quandoEvitar: Use `donut-chart` or `composition-chart` when there are many small categories: below half a percent, a category may end up with no cell.
Use `bar-chart` to compare values that don't add up to a whole.
Use `progress` or `usage-meter` for a single fraction, such as quota usage.

teclado.acao: With focus on the grid, move up or down one cell in the column and read its category.
Move to the neighboring cell, in the previous or next column.
Page Down jumps to the start of the next category; Page Up returns to the start of the current one or, if already there, of the previous one.
Go to the first or last filled cell.
Ends the reading and hides the tooltip.
In the legend, pin or release the category's highlight.

acessibilidade: The grid is a focusable group with `aria-roledescription="waffle chart"` and the instructions in its name, in English; an `aria-live="polite"` region reads the current cell's category with share and value.
The legend is a list of buttons with `aria-pressed`; a hidden summary and table carry each category's value, share, and number of cells.
Cell shape is a second channel besides color: apart from the highlighted category, categories alternate between square, round, and framed, and the legend repeats the shape.
movimento: On entering the viewport, cells grow and appear in a short wave, in fill order: bottom to top, column by column.
When the data changes, cells that change group or position fly to the new place, shrinking mid-flight, and change color and shape along the way; the legend percentages roll.
With “reduced motion” on, cells go straight to their final place and color and the percentages swap without rolling.
responsivo: In a container of 420 px or more, the legend sits beside the grid; below that, it drops to a one-column list.
The grid is at most 300 px wide (232 px with the legend beside it) and the cells follow that measure; on touch, dragging horizontally scans the cells and the vertical gesture scrolls the page.
desempenho: Each cell is an animated element with `will-change: transform`: the default grid has 100, and larger `rows` × `columns` multiply that number.
notasIA: Pass `data` as `{ key, label, value }` in fill order, with raw values: slices are computed and rounded to whole cells that always sum to the grid (10 × 10, one percent each).
Keep `key` stable between datasets so cells fly instead of repainting; `unit` and `formatValue` format the tooltip and table, and `decimals` the percentages.
The accent color goes to `accentKey` (the first category, by default) and the next three use the other series colors; `activeKey` with `onActiveChange` controls the pinned category.
